Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

accessibility 1.6.0

New features

  • cumulative_interval() has a new argument fill_missing_ids. When TRUE (the default), ids that reach no opportunity are kept with accessibility 0, as in cumulative_cutoff().

Major changes

  • Accessibility functions now treat NA opportunity, demand and supply values, and travel_matrix ids missing from land_use_data, as 0. Previously, they could make results NA.
  • Integer opportunity, demand, supply and population columns are now converted to doubles, so sums no longer overflow. As a result, cumulative_cutoff() and gravity() (with decay_binary()) return doubles instead of integers when opportunities are integers.
  • concentration_index(type = "corrected") now uses the bounds of the whole accessibility distribution, not of each group_by group, to calculate the correction factor.
  • cumulative_interval() no longer truncates results to integers (e.g. a median of 26.5).
  • constrained_accessibility(constraint = "doubly") now always returns origin-destination flows and ignores active and detailed_results. Previously, detailed_results = FALSE returned the demand and supply marginals instead (#67).

Bug fixes

  • balancing_cost(): numeric ids were used as positions to look up population, returning NA or wrong costs; origins balanced only when opportunities exceeded (instead of matched) population; and costs above the last multiple of cost_increment were NA. cost_increment must now be greater than 0.
  • concentration_index(): tied incomes now share the same fractional rank, so results no longer depend on row order. With type = "corrected", the index is now 0, instead of NaN, when everyone has the same accessibility.
  • concentration_index(), gini_index() and theil_t() no longer return NA due to integer overflow with large opportunity and population counts.
  • constrained_accessibility():
    • constraint = "doubly" aligned impedances and totals by row position instead of by id; pairs missing from travel_matrix are now unreachable.
    • constraint = "doubly" no longer adds a constant to the balancing factors, which distorted results with very small weights, and now warns when balancing stops before reaching error_threshold.
    • constraint = "doubly" now returns the same class as travel_matrix.
    • constraint = "total" or "singly" no longer errors when fill_missing_ids = TRUE and group_by leave combinations missing.
    • constraint = "total" no longer adds an index to the user’s land_use_data.
    • constraint = "total", "singly" and "doubly" now treat each group_by combination and each decay value as an independent system. Previously, "total" split the regional total across groups, "doubly" balanced all groups as a single system, and all three blended several decay values into one result. Detailed results now keep the group_by and decay_function_arg columns (#66, @soukhova).
  • cost_to_closest() no longer returns Inf due to integer overflow with large opportunity counts.
  • cumulative_cutoff(): cutoffs with floating point noise (e.g. from seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.1)) could be zeroed when filling missing ids. Travel cost columns with non-syntactic names now work.
  • cumulative_interval(): cutoffs with floating point noise (e.g. from interval_increment = 0.1) were left out of the summary.
  • decay_stepped() no longer warns for each NA travel cost.
  • palma_ratio(): income cutoffs depended on the scale of population (NA with population shares), and with several group_by columns the output included NA rows for absent combinations. The output is no longer keyed.
  • spatial_availability(): a destination no one could reach made all results NaN. Its opportunities are now left unallocated.
  • theil_t(): observations with no access are now included and contribute 0 (0 * log(0) = 0), instead of being excluded or making the index NaN. group_by levels where no one has access are kept with NA.

Minor changes

  • Errors and warnings now use cli. cli and rlang are new dependencies.
  • Accessibility, inequality and poverty functions now raise an error if land_use_data or sociodemographic_data have duplicated ids.
  • Accessibility functions:
    • raise an error on negative travel costs and a clear error when the id types of travel_matrix and land_use_data are incompatible.
    • match land use data by id with match(), making them about 1.2 to 3.3 times faster with half the memory. A travel_matrix column named like the opportunity column is now replaced.
    • no longer return keyed data.tables when filling missing ids.
  • Several functions are faster on large travel matrices. Results may differ from previous versions by floating point rounding only.
  • balancing_cost(), cumulative_cutoff() and cumulative_interval() are about 4 to 20 times faster, because opportunities are summed once per travel cost instead of once per cutoff.
  • constrained_accessibility() checks that demand and supply are single strings. With constraint = "doubly", it is about 2 to 4 times faster and uses much less memory.
  • cost_to_closest() is about 1.3 to 2.3 times faster.
  • cumulative_interval() always sorts rows by interval, id and group_by.
  • decay_exponential(), decay_logistic(), decay_power() and decay_stepped() are about 2 to 200 times faster.
  • decay_linear() requires cutoff greater than 0.
  • decay_logistic() and decay_stepped() raise an error on duplicated parameter combinations.
  • fgt_poverty() raises an error on invalid poverty_line or poor_below_threshold, and warns when poor_below_threshold = FALSE and accessibility_data has Inf values (e.g. from cost_to_closest()).
  • floating_catchment_area() and gravity() are faster with several decay values (about 4 times with three).
  • spatial_availability() is about 2 times faster.

Notes

  • Updated URLs after the repository moved from ipeaGIT to ipea.

accessibility 1.5.0

CRAN release: 2026-05-12

New features

  • New function constrained_accessibility(), which implements the family of constrained accessibility measures proposed in Soukhov et al. (2025).

Minor changes

  • The function fgt_poverty() has a new argument poor_below_threshold. When set to TRUE (default) the observations below the poverty line are considered to be poor. This is the correct approach for primal accessibility measures (e.g. cumulative accessibility). If FALSE, then observations above the poverty line are considered to be poor. This is the correct approach for dual accessibility measures (e.g. travel time to the closest facility). When set to FALSE, FGT 1 and 2 do not have an upper bound. Closes #63

accessibility 1.4.0

CRAN release: 2024-03-06

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a bug in which land use data passed to accessibility functions as a tibble could lead to an error.

New features

  • New function decay_logistic().

Notes

  • Package description has been adjusted to better reflect the current set of available features.

accessibility 1.3.0

CRAN release: 2023-10-20

New features

  • New parameter detailed_results to spatial_availability(), used to specify whether results should be aggregated by origin-destination pair or by origin. When aggregating by origin-destination pair, the output also includes the demand, impedance and combined balancing factors used to calculate spatial availability.

accessibility 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2023-09-21

New features

  • New inequality functions concentration_index() and theil_t().

Notes

  • Various documentation tweaks.
  • Testing performance has greatly improved.

accessibility 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2023-06-22

New features

  • The package now includes functions to estimate accessibility inequalities (palma_ratio() and gini_index()) and poverty (fgt_poverty()).
  • New accessibility functions spatial_availability() and balancing_cost().
  • New vignette “Calculating accessibility inequality and poverty”.
  • cost_to_closest() parameter n now accepts a numeric vector, instead of being restricted to a single number.
  • cumulative_cutoff() parameters cutoff and travel_cost now accepts a numeric and a character vector, respectively, instead of being restricted to a single number/string.
  • cumulative_interval() parameter interval now accepts a list of numeric vectors, instead of being restricted to a single vector.
  • The decay functions can now take numeric vectors as input, instead of being restricted to a single number (in the case of decay_stepped(), both steps and weights can take a list of numeric vectors as input, instead of being restricted to a single numeric vector each).

Notes

  • Various documentation tweaks.
  • Added the new accessibility functions to the intro vignette.

accessibility 1.0.1

CRAN release: 2022-10-06

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a bug in which cost_to_closest() would return NA values when filling missing ids (which should be filled with Inf, since they cannot reach any opportunities). This was also responsible for the warning reported in #27, which was also fixed.

accessibility 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2022-07-22

The package has been through tremendous changes. Basically, there’s not a single part of it that remained untouched: documentation, vignettes, function names, parameter names, extra functionality, performance improvements, etc. While it is impossible to highlight everything that has been done, we’ll try to summarize some of the key points in the following topics.

Breaking changes

  • Accessibility functions previously worked with a single input dataset: data. Now they require two input datasets: travel_matrix and land_use_data.
  • Function names were changed:
    • time_to_closest() -> cost_to_closest()
    • cumulative_time_cutoff() -> cumulative_cutoff()
    • cumulative_time_interval() -> cumulative_interval()
    • gravity_access() -> gravity()
  • Parameter names were changed:
    • opportunity_col -> opportunity
    • travel_cost_col -> travel_cost
    • by_col -> active
    • In cost_to_closest(): n_opportunities -> n
    • In cumulative_interval(): stat -> summary_function
    • In floating_catchment_area(): population_col -> demand
    • In floating_catchment_area(): fca_metric -> method
  • Parameter required values were changed:
    • active now takes a logical, instead of a string (which by_col previously took).
    • In cumulative_interval(): summary_function now takes a function, instead of a string (which stat previously took).

New features

  • New function decay_stepped().
  • New parameter interval_increment to cumulative_interval(), used to specify how many travel cost units separate the cutoffs used to calculate the accessibility estimates which will be used to calculate the summary estimate within the specified interval.
  • All accessibility functions gained a group_by parameter, that allows accessibility estimates to be grouped by one or more columns present in travel_matrix.
  • All accessibility functions (but cumulative_interval()) gained a fill_missing_ids parameter, that includes in the results origins whose accessibility would be 0 but, due to some commonly overlooked implementation details, are usually left out from the output. cumulative_interval() doesn’t have this parameter because its result will always include all origins, otherwise the summary measure wouldn’t be calculated properly.
